newsitem.title: UK: LME nickel, aluminium steam higher, more gains see.
newsitem.headline: LME nickel, aluminium steam higher, more gains see.

text.p: LME nickel and aluminium closed on Monday with robust gains after touching fresh nine-month highs in the morning and taking a breather in the afternoon.
Copper also extended its recent rise, touching a fresh peak, although volumes were not big, traders said.
Three months nickel finished the kerb at $8,085 per tonne, a rise of $210 on the day, after earlier hitting a high of $8,110.
"Nickel did great guns today and has potential for more. There's a bit of resistance from $8,050 to $8,110, but if we can close over $8,130, we'll be on track for $8,400," a senior trader said.

Monday's move was the strongest price since May 30, 1996, when the market hit $8,150, helped by news that unpaid workers at Norilsk Nickel will discuss on March 1 the possibility of taking action to disrupt output.
The Norilsk news pushed prices above the benchmark $8,000 level, where stops were hit.
Aluminium also surged to the highest levels since last June, hitting a peak of $1,661 as technical buying overpowered resistance.
The market saw some forward selling and borrowing, which pushed prices off their highs, but it still ended with an impressive $23 gain at $1,654.
The close was even more positive since it held prices above a key chart point of $1,651/2, traders said.
Copper also carved out a fresh peak since June 1996 of $2,385, but profit-taking knocked it back on the kerb below $2,375 resistance.
Most analysts are still bullish of copper in the short-term, with tightness emerging in April dates and analysts point to a target of $2,450 based on a ascending triangle.
Some of the other metals explored higher levels, but failed to sustain them.
Zinc touched $1,220, but ended only $5 firmer at $1,216, continuing a consolidation phase.
Lead ended $2 firmer at $671 and tin finished the day $5 higher at $5,985 after briefly looking at $6,020.
